text:
sara: Hey team — just received my company MacBook (M2, macOS 13.6). Trying to do the MDM enrollment during first-boot but it keeps failing with 'Profile verification failed'. I tried the office Wi‑Fi and my phone hotspot, same error. Anyone know what to try?

it-support: Hey @sara — sorry about that. Can you paste the serial number and the exact error screenshot (if any)? Quick check: are you on the captive portal for guest wifi, or the corp SSID?

sara: Serial is C02XXXXXXX. Screenshot: "Profile verification failed: Unable to verify the identity of the server." I'm definitely on our corp SSID (redwood-secure) and it asks for certs.

it-support: Thanks. That error usually means the device can't validate the MDM TLS cert chain during DEP/Automated Enrollment. Two quick possibilities: (1) the corp Wi‑Fi is intercepting/blocking the enrollment flow (proxy/captive), or (2) local date/time is wrong so cert validation fails. Can you check System Settings -> General -> Date & Time and confirm auto-set is on?

sara: Date/time was correct and auto-set was on. I also tried with my phone hotspot (no proxy) and still same error.

james: @it-support fyi, our Apple Business Manager logs show the serial as Unassigned (never completed DEP enrollment). Could be the profile step failing before device is marked.

it-support: Ok. @sara two more tries: 1) Try enrolling manually via the enrollment URL we sent in the welcome email (Settings -> Profiles -> Install profile). 2) If manual install fails, try a temporary reinstall of macOS via Internet Recovery (Cmd+Option+R) to clear any half-applied profiles, then attempt enrollment on the corp Wi‑Fi again. If you don't want to reinstall, try this command in terminal to force profile download and give us the output: 

```bash
sudo profiles renew -type enrollment
```

sara: Ran the command. Output: "profiles: The system policy prevented the execution of the command." (I don't have admin).

emily: Hey @sara — new hires don't get local admin by default. If IT needs admin for troubleshooting, we can grant temporary sudo for 24h. Want me to approve?

sara: Yes please, that would help.

it-support: @emily please grant temporary admin, then @sara run that command and paste output. If it still fails, we'll ask you to join a quick Zoom so we can try Apple Configurator steps.

emily: Approved temporary admin for @sara for 24h.

sara: Re-ran `sudo profiles renew -type enrollment` — output now: "Enrollment request failed: TLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed (unable to get local issuer certificate)"

it-support: That's the cert chain issue. @james can you check the MDM cert expiry/chain? Also, @sara can you try connecting to a wired ethernet (USB-C -> gigabit adapter) if available — sometimes corporate wifi does a proxy that interferes even if it looks fine.

james: Looking at the MDM server: intermediate cert was missing from the chain on one of our LB nodes — rolled a fix a few minutes ago. If you reboot and try again that should help, but caches can stick. @sara can you reboot and try the enrollment URL again?

sara: Rebooted and clicked the enrollment link from the welcome email. It prompted for install, then completed! On Profiles it shows "Redwood MDM: Enrolled" and Device appears in ABM. All good. Thanks everyone. :tada:

it-support: Nice — thanks for hanging in there. For the record, we'll follow up with a short postmortem on the cert chain deploy so new hires don't hit this.

devops-oncall: Leaving a note: if anyone else hits a cert verify error during org enroll, try phone hotspot as a quick isolation step and ping #eng-infra so we can check LB cert chains immediately.

sara: One follow-up — FileVault setup didn't prompt during enrollment. I did System Settings -> Privacy & Security -> FileVault and it says 'Turn On FileVault'. Do new hires need to rotate recovery keys to our KMS?

it-support: Good catch. We usually let users enable FileVault and then run a small script to escrow the personal recovery key to our KMS. @it-support will push a one-time post-enroll job, but if you want to enable now please do and then reply here so we can confirm escrow was captured.

sara: Enabled FileVault, it restarted and completed encryption. Let me know if you see the key escrows.

it-support: Confirmed — recovery key escrowed to KMS. All set. Welcome aboard, @sara!

emily: Welcome again! Ping us in #new-hires if anything else pops up. :)
